issues.target: recommend_result.json current_state_verdict ('The limit is the serial loop body under lockstep ... It is not the ring'); baseline/README.md 'What changed in the conclusions' bullet 1
issues.problem: The stated root cause does not add up. The quoted medians (retrieve 10.1-10.3 + put_frame 3.6-3.7 + record_frame 1.1-1.2 ms) sum to 14.8-15.2 ms, which is UNDER the 16.7 ms budget. The finalizer breakdown in the same run shows 15.77 ms median processing plus 2.49 ms median camera idle (13.6%), i.e. the lockstep gate wait is about 2.5 ms per frame. put_frame alone is 23.1% of processing time in the e2e loop, so 'it is not the ring' contradicts the e2e data. The isolated a_write 353 fps figure does not represent the in-loop cost (3.56 ms in e2e vs 2.75 ms isolated).
issues.fix: Restate: at 5x1080p mjpeg the loop body is about 15.8 ms and the lockstep gate adds about 2.5 ms idle (max-of-5 cameras + 0.53 ms wait_10us granularity), giving 18.7 ms. Both put_frame (3.6 ms) and the gate (2.5 ms) are each large enough to decide whether 60 fps is met. Re-weigh ranks 8 and 12 accordingly, and measure rank 8 alone in the real stack (bench_e_e2e.py with copy.copy patched out in the benchmark process).

Arithmetic 10.1+3.6+1.1=14.8, 10.3+3.7+1.2=15.2. issues.target: recommend_result.json headline and rank 6 expected_impact (59.95 fps, 0 lost, vs 53.56 at HEAD)
issues.problem: The prototype that produced 59.95 fps is not the design being recommended and skips real SkellyCam steps. P8 has no lockstep gate (rank 6 keeps lockstep: 'The camera loop then sets frame_count ... so the encoder no longer gates lockstep'), no camera_loop_update_checks/pubsub polling per frame, no 632 B recarray metadata and ~31 nested timestamp writes (0.42 ms by their own micro-bench), no start/stop recording handshake, no RecordingFinalizer, and a reduced UI build (no SkellyCam payload format, builds only when all cameras have a new frame). Free-running cameras with random phase also give up the grab-time sync that the current design exists for, and P8 measured no cross-camera spread. The recommended configuration (lockstep + decoupled recorder + seqlock) was never measured end to end.
issues.fix: Label the headline as 'prototype without lockstep and without SkellyCam loop overheads'. Add one P8 variant that keeps a lockstep gate (shared frame_count array + the same wait policy) and the SkellyCam per-frame metadata writes, and report the cross-camera grab spread (as bench_e_e2e does) before claiming that rank 6 restores 60 fps.
issues.evidence: prototypes/p8_e2e_proto.py docstring L8-9 ('No lockstep gate, no encode, no copy.copy, no private recarray') and camera() L128-170 (loop has no gate and no update checks); ui_relay L289-293 (skip unless all heads advanced). prototypes_result.json limitations[1]. Baseline loop with those steps: opencv_camera_loop.py L43-117 (https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_camera_loop.py#L43-L117). e2e finalizer: 'Idle before copy to camera SHM 0.445 ms', 'Idle before frame record 0.123 ms' (e_e2e_1080p_mjpeg_ui.json). cpp/results/micro_py.json skellycam_nested_recarray_timestamp_write 13,502 ns.

issues.target: All 5x60 e2e numbers (baseline bench_e_e2e FakeCapture, P8 FakeSensor) as a model of real cameras
issues.problem: The synthetic camera model is contradicted by the only real-camera measurement. FakeCapture.grab() blocks until the next sensor tick and retrieve() only decodes; on real DSHOW cameras grab() returns in 0.00-0.01 ms and retrieve() takes about 32 ms (wait + decode). Real retrieve CPU is 11.0-14.7 ms per 1080p frame (at 30 fps), versus about 7.3 ms (isolated) to 10.1 ms (in e2e) for the imdecode stand-in. If the real per-frame CPU on the calling thread is near 13 ms, the decode-in-loop design of rank 6 has about 3-4 ms of headroom, not about 7 ms. The recommendation lists 'which stand-in a real camera resembles' as open, but it still presents 59.95 fps and 53.56 fps as the expected real outcome without this caveat.
issues.fix: Put the P9 contradiction next to every 5x60 number. Re-run P8 with a stand-in whose grab() returns at once and whose retrieve() waits for the tick and then decodes. Add a CPU-cost stand-in calibrated to P9's 11-15 ms/frame at 1080p. State that per-frame decode CPU on real cameras at 60 fps is unmeasured.
issues.evidence: baseline/bench_e_e2e.py FakeCapture L57-99 (grab blocks in _next_tick; retrieve = imdecode + copyto). prototypes/results/p9_real_camera.md: grab median 0.00 ms, retrieve+publish median 31.97-34.55 ms, CPU ms/frame 10.95-14.69 at 1920x1080 (all 4 cameras). baseline/results/g_decode_ref.md (imdecode 1080p 7.30 ms 1 proc); e_e2e_summary.md retrieve median 10.12 ms. Script: prototypes/p9_real_camera.py.

issues.target: recommend_result.json rank 4 (gap detector: missed = max(0, round(interval / expected_period) - 1)); expected_impact 'Makes the dominant loss mode visible'
issues.problem: The proposed formula cannot see the measured dominant loss mode. At HEAD 5x1080p mjpeg the grab interval is 18.67 ms median and 22.04 ms p99 at a 16.67 ms period: round(18.67/16.67)-1 = 0 and round(22.04/16.67)-1 = 0. Only intervals of 25 ms or more (under 1% of frames) would count, so the detector would report at most a few frames per camera out of the 192-193 per camera that were actually never grabbed. Losses spread as a 1.12x slower cadence are invisible to per-interval rounding.
issues.fix: Count against an accumulated clock: missed_total = round((t_last - t_first) / period) + 1 - frames, or accumulate fractional (interval/period - 1) and take the floor of the sum. Better still, use device pts where available. Validate the detector offline against the baseline e2e per-frame timestamps (CAPTURED_METADATA), where the true answer (964) is known.
issues.evidence: baseline/results/e_e2e_1080p_mjpeg_ui.json per_camera.*.grab_interval: median 18.665-18.70 ms, p99 22.04-22.07 ms, max 41.1-42.8 ms; sensor_frames_never_grabbed 192-193 per camera. Arithmetic: round(18.67/16.667)=1, round(22.04/16.667)=1. Proposed code location opencv_camera_loop.py L80-84 (https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_camera_loop.py#L80-L84).

issues.target: P1 claim 'No grabbed frame was lost on the way to disk' (recommend current_state_verdict, baseline_result findings[1]); all record/e2e 'disk MB/s' figures
issues.problem: No benchmark measured the physical disk. No script calls fsync/FlushFileBuffers or uses unbuffered I/O. Recordings (about 2.1 GB per e2e run, 0.7-2.3 GB per c_record row, 4.9 GB per P4 passthrough row) fit in the 64 GB page cache, are re-read from cache to count frames, and are then deleted. 'disk MB/s 5166' for unthrottled passthrough (P4) is page-cache throughput. What the tests show is that the writer API accepted every frame. They do not show that the disk keeps up or that the data is durable. Long recordings and full-disk behaviour were not tested: the C: volume had 225.6 GB free (94.4% used) on 20261027, which is about 23 min at P4's synthetic 162 MB/s or about 48 min at the MSMF e2e 69 MB/s. The recommendation quotes '91% full per research.json', which is the stale 2026-10-25 value.
issues.fix: Reword the P1 statement to 'the writer accepted every grabbed frame (OS cache)'. Add a sustained-write test: at least 10 min at the target rate, with FlushFileBuffers at stop, and a run larger than RAM or with the standby list purged. Report time-to-disk-full, and add a free-space guard to the plan. Update the disk-fill figure from environment_system.json.
issues.evidence: Grep for fsync|FlushFileBuffers|FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING|O_DIRECT over research/frame_ring_buffer/**/*.py: no matches. baseline/bench_e_e2e.py L263-302 (VideoCapture counts, then shutil.rmtree at L337). prototypes/p8_e2e_proto.py L355-360 (count then unlink). e_e2e_1080p_mjpeg_ui.json recording_total_bytes 2,081,764,275. prototypes/results/p4_mjpeg_passthrough.md 'disk MB/s' 162.1 / 5166.3. baseline/results/environment_system.json temp_volume SizeRemaining 225,607,315,456 of 3,999,610,695,680. recommend open_questions[4] ('91% full per research.json').

issues.target: recommend_result.json rank 11 expected_impact (60.1 payloads/s vs 51.8/s; build off the event loop)
issues.problem: The payload-rate gain comes from the poll interval, not from views or the thread pool. With the same 10 ms poll, view_proto_threads gives 46.4 payloads/s, which is LOWER than cur_copy_real (51.8/s). Only the 2 ms poll variant reaches 60.1/s, and the baseline no-sleep run already reached 60.0 distinct/s with the current build. P6 rates are also single 10 s runs with large timer-phase noise: the same variant measured 60.0 vs 42.6/s (720p) and 53.0 vs 57.8/s (1080p) across two venvs, and cur_copy_real (51.8/s) differs from the baseline d_ui measurement of the same path (46.0/s). Only the event-loop-blocking reduction (8.28 -> 0.04 ms) is a robust result.
issues.fix: Split rank 11 into (a) poll faster or wake on an event, which gives the rate, and (b) build in a thread pool from views, which removes event-loop blocking. Quote 46.4/s for (b) alone. Repeat P6 rows at least 3x, or align the poll to a timer, before quoting payloads/s differences under about 30%.

issues.target: recommend_result.json rank 9 expected_impact ('Output (124.9 Mbit/s) and encode rate (114.7 vs 115.4 fps unthrottled) are unchanged')
issues.problem: The recommended setting is setNumThreads(1), but the unthrottled encode-rate comparison was run only for default vs 2 threads. No unthrottled row exists for 1 thread, so MSMF throughput headroom at threads=1 is unmeasured. The paced 60 fps rows show threads=1 keeps up on an otherwise idle machine, with record_frame rising from 2.16 to 2.42 ms. P10 is also provisional (Defender scan).

issues.target: recommend_result.json rank 7 expected_impact ('a 1 GiB compressed ring ... holds about 9,250 frames, about 154 s') and evidence ('3 of 4 real cameras: 100% FF D8 packets')
issues.problem: (1) The prototype that was actually measured used fixed 1 MiB JPEG slots, 1024 slots per camera, which is about 17 s at 60 fps, not 154 s. The 9,250-frame figure assumes a variable-size packed ring that was never built. (2) The PyAV dshow capture path was refused at 60 fps on every camera and size except c922 720p, and that one delivered 30.1 fps. Without an explicit framerate option, the c922 and C930e negotiated 10 fps raw (0 of 31 FF D8 packets). '3 of 4 cameras deliver JPEG' holds only at 30 fps with an explicit framerate option, so a 60 fps passthrough capture is shown on no device.
issues.fix: State the stall budget of the design that was built (1024 x 1 MiB = 17 s), or prototype a packed variable-size ring before claiming 154 s. Qualify the P9b evidence as '30 fps with an explicit framerate option only. 60 fps open failed (I/O error) on 7 of 8 device/size combinations.'

issues.target: recommend_result.json rank 6 ('A thread in the camera process is enough (MSMF write releases the GIL: P7 x1.64 threads vs x1.53 processes)')
issues.problem: P7 compares 5 MSMF writers as threads in one process against 5 processes. It does not measure a recorder thread sharing a process (and the GIL) with a Python capture loop. P8, the only e2e evidence for rank 6, used a separate recorder process per camera. The thread topology is therefore unmeasured.
issues.fix: Mark the thread option as an estimate, or add a P8 variant with the recorder as a thread in the camera process and report grab-interval p99 and never-grabbed counts.

issues.target: recommend_result.json rank 5 expected_impact ('Removes silent torn reads: the current pattern accepted 15 to about 41,800 tears per 10 s')
issues.problem: The tears come from an emulation of the current pattern on SeqRing, not the real class, driven by an unthrottled 4,300 fps writer, with 2- and 8-slot rings or reads of the oldest slot. With SkellyCam's real ring length (388 at 720p) and 'latest' reads, the current pattern showed 0 tears. At 60 fps a latest read would have to stall for about (L-1) x 16.7 ms = 6.4 s to tear. The real tear risk is for lagging by-index readers (FreeMoCap), and the gating/counting benefit, not tear-proofing, is what justifies rank 5. Also, the '0 torn in 50 SPSC runs' evidence cited for the seqlock comes from gated SPSC runs, where the writer can never overwrite an unread slot, so it does not exercise the seqlock.
issues.fix: Quote the L=388 latest row (0 tears for the current pattern) alongside the adversarial rows. Name the realistic tear scenario (FreeMoCap get_data_by_index of a frame (L-1) behind head). Cite P2 part A, not the gated SPSC runs, as the seqlock evidence.

issues.target: recommend_result.json cpp_verdict ('Codec speed is set by the OpenCV / libjpeg-turbo build')
issues.problem: The verdict leaves out the same-version comparison. At OpenCV 4.8.0, C++ decodes 1080p in 11.32 ms (copy) or 10.36 ms (in place, dst=) against 12.78 ms in Python: 11-19% faster on the largest per-frame cost. The cpp README says this gap cannot be attributed (the two 4.8 builds differ), but a C++ build linked to libjpeg-turbo 3.x with in-place decode was not measured, so 'would not raise throughput meaningfully' is not proven for decode.
issues.fix: Add the same-version numbers and list 'C++ in-place decode with a current libjpeg-turbo' as an untested option, alongside C1 and C4.

issues.target: recommend_result.json current_state_verdict / rank 4 ('SkellyCam cannot see that loss')
issues.problem: Overstated. The finalizer printed 'Mean Framerate 53.93 Hz' for a 60 fps configuration, which does expose a 10% shortfall. What is true is that validate_recording does not check the rate or gaps and passes.
issues.fix: Say 'the loss is not counted or validated (validate_recording checks file counts only); it is visible only as a lower mean framerate in the stats'.

issues.target: Machine-state control across all stages (idle rule, hybrid CPU)
issues.problem: The idle rule is a share of all 28 logical CPUs, so one fully busy background thread (3.6%) passes it. The i7-14700K is a hybrid part (8 P-cores + 12 E-cores). No run pinned affinity or recorded which core type the camera/decoder/encoder threads ran on, and the power plan was Balanced. Decode times can differ substantially between P- and E-cores, which may contribute to unexplained run-to-run variance (e.g. P6 timer-phase variance, b_read round medians).
issues.fix: Record per-process core-type residency, or pin to P-cores for one repeat of the key rows (baseline 1080p mjpeg e2e, P8 1080p imdecode msmf). Report the per-thread maximum background load, not only the machine-wide share.
issues.evidence: baseline/README.md environment ('20 cores / 28 threads', power plan Balanced); baseline/run_with_load.py idle rule (background mean/p95 < 10% of the whole machine); baseline/README.md 'Read-style round variance ... cause was not established'.

issues.target: Baseline e2e UI consumer (bench_e_e2e.py ui_task) as evidence for UI cost and rank 1 risk
issues.problem: The e2e UI is a stand-in. It catches every exception instead of setting global_kill_flag, has no websocket send, deflate or ack, and skips the relay's framerate trackers. The measured 'UI costs capture 53.56 vs 55.94 fps' is therefore a lower bound from 1 no-UI run. Fault behaviour (rank 1) was structurally excluded from the e2e runs rather than observed as absent.
issues.fix: State in the verdict that the e2e UI path cannot trigger the kill path. Add the fault-injection test already proposed in rank 1(e) as a benchmark, and repeat the no-UI run.

summary: Most cited numbers match their output files: e2e 53.56/53.57 fps and 964 never grabbed, P8 59.95 fps, P1 copy.copy 3.085 -> 1.166 ms, cpp ring and VideoWriter CPU sums (382/397/443 vs 1127/1257/1279%), P3 stall table, and P9 0.30-1.38 ms in-place savings. The C++ vs Python comparison is fair: it controls for the OpenCV version with a cv2 4.8 venv. The recommendations rest, however, on several weak inferences. (1) The root-cause arithmetic is wrong. The quoted loop medians sum to 14.8-15.2 ms, under the 16.7 ms budget, and the finalizer shows 2.5 ms of lockstep idle, with put_frame at 23% of the loop. So both the gate and the ring matter, and 'it is not the ring' contradicts the e2e data. (2) The 59.95 fps headline comes from a prototype that drops lockstep and SkellyCam's per-frame overheads, while the recommended design keeps lockstep and was never measured. (3) The synthetic camera model (grab blocks, retrieve decodes) is contradicted by P9 on real DSHOW (grab 0 ms, retrieve 32 ms, 11-15 ms CPU at 1080p). (4) The rank-4 gap formula, round(interval/period)-1, returns 0 for the measured 18.7 ms intervals and would miss nearly all 964 lost frames. (5) No test touched the physical disk (no fsync, files in page cache, then deleted), and the disk is 94.4% full (225.6 GB), not 91%. (6) The rank-11 rate gain comes from the 2 ms poll, not from views or threads (46.4/s with threads at a 10 ms poll), and the P6 noise is ±15-30%. (7) The rank-9 'encode rate unchanged' was measured for 2 threads, not the recommended 1. (8) The rank-7 154 s ring budget assumes a packed ring that was never built (the prototype held 17 s), and PyAV dshow refused 60 fps on 7 of 8 device/size combinations. Smaller problems: a wrong FreeMoCap line ref for kill_everything (L351, not L256-280), deflate timings cited from the wrong temp file, a tear-risk framing that ignores the 0-tear result at the real ring length, and no control for P-core/E-core placement. No new benchmarks were run in this stage, so there was no machine load to record.
